subject: Initial-packet guarantee waiver request for Cedar POC (CH-4421)
messages:
From: Emily Stein <emily.stein@cedarhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Cedar Health Procurement <procurement@cedarhealth.com>
Date: 2028-06-15T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Request: initial-packet guarantee waiver for Cedar POC (CH-4421)

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the model quality looks promising. As we ramp the POC traffic against our ingestion pipeline, we observed a pattern that makes the standard streaming time-to-first-token (TTFT) and sustained-token/sec commitments difficult to meet for a subset of calls. I attached a small sample of the traffic (POC_traffic_patterns.csv) and our internal SLO expectations (SLO_summary.pdf).

What we’re seeing: a) roughly 12% of POC requests are single-shot but carry very long contexts (1k-2k tokens) and b) about 8% of requests are highly bursty in a short window (concurrent spikes to 200+ streams for 10–30s). These are real user scenarios for our diagnostics feature.

As Cedar Health’s procurement lead, I need to propose a pragmatic SLA carving: temporary waiver that relaxes the TTFT commitment for the "initial packet" (first 1–2 tokens) for requests that meet either of the two risk patterns above. Proposed acceptance criteria:
- Waiver window: 90-day POC only (no production SLA change)
- Allowed TTFT on waived requests: up to 1.5s for the initial packet; regular TTFT applies otherwise
- Sustained token rate: allow initial 3s bursts up to 120 tokens/sec, with a 60s rolling average target of 40 tokens/sec
- Monitoring & rollback: Cedar to share load profile; Redwood to provide p95 TTFT and token-rate reporting; automatic rollback if error rate increases > 2% over baseline.

Can Redwood provide a formal carveout/waiver that includes operational guards (timebox, metrics, and an agreed fallback model) and confirm impacts on pricing (we expect an estimate for dedicated warm capacity or a commit to throttle/burst controls)?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement would like a proposal to include in our internal approval packet next week.

Best,
Emily
Emily Stein
Head of Procurement | Cedar Health
Attachments: POC_traffic_patterns.csv (text/csv), SLO_summary.pdf (application/pdf)

Thanks for looping me in. My initial technical proposal to minimize risk while meeting Cedar's ask:

1) Scope & duration- POC-only waiver, 60 days (we can extend to 90 days by mutual agreement).

2) TTFT carveout definition (for clarity):
- \"Initial packet\" = time from request accept to first token byte emitted.
- Waived path applies only when incoming request has >1024 input tokens OR when concurrent active streams exceed 150 for a given endpoint.
- Allowed TTFT on waived path: up to 1.5 seconds (p95 during waiver window).

3) Token/sec / burst rules:
- Allow initial 3s burst up to 120 tokens/sec per stream for waived calls; enforce a 60s rolling average target of 40 tokens/sec per stream.
- If 60s rolling average exceeds 60 tokens/sec for a stream, apply best-effort throttling and emit a negotiated warning header to the client.

4) Operational mitigations:
- Provision a small dedicated warm pool for Cedar's POC endpoints (configurable size; recommend 4x baseline concurrency).
- Pre-warm KV caches for known prompts (customer can provide top 200 prompt prefixes).
- Automatic fallback: if error rate >2% or sustained p95 TTFT >2s for 10 minutes, route to a quantized smaller model (approx -2 FL ops) to preserve throughput while degrading token quality gracefully.

5) Metrics & reporting:
- We will report: p50/p95 TTFT, median tokens/sec, 60s rolling average tokens/sec, request error-rate, and dropped-stream counts every 10 minutes.
- Logs retained for 30 days for the POC (can extend with add-on).

6) Billing & exposure:
- Estimate: dedicated warm capacity for 60-day POC (4x concurrency) ~ $15k–$25k depending on run-hours; fallback usage billed at standard rate.

These limits keep the waiver tightly scoped and give us clear rollback conditions. Happy to convert into the draft language for the procurement doc.

—Vivek

Emily — thanks for the sample and the clear ask. Please find our provisional waiver proposal below (attached as redwood-waiver-proposal-CH4421.pdf). Summary and next steps: 

1) Term & scope: 60-day POC-only waiver for the named Cedar endpoints (we can extend to 90 days at mutual agreement).

2) TTFT & token-rate carveout:
- Waiver applies to \"initial packet\" as defined by Vivek when requests have >1024 context tokens or when endpoint concurrency >150.
- Allowed p95 TTFT on waived calls: up to 1.5s.
- Initial 3s per-stream burst allowed up to 120 tokens/sec; 60s rolling average target of 40 tokens/sec per stream.

3) Operational controls:
- Redwood will provision a dedicated warm pool (estimate attached).
- Pre-warm/cache top prefixes (we’ll share a short list for prefetch).
- Fallback: automated routing to quantized model if error-rate or sustained TTFT thresholds breached.

4) Monitoring & rollback:
- Metrics: p50/p95 TTFT, median tokens/sec, 60s rolling average, error-rate.
- Automatic rollback trigger: error-rate >2% above baseline for 10 continuous minutes or sustained p95 TTFT >2s for 10 continuous minutes.

5) Commercials:
- Estimated incremental cost for 60-day warm capacity: $18,500 (ballpark) — final quote pending exact run-hours.
- Waiver limited to POC endpoints; no change to base SLA for other endpoints.

6) Next steps:
- Review attached PDF. If you’re aligned, please sign the DocuSign link (https://docusign.redwood.com/CH-4421) and we’ll kick off provisioning and share dashboard access within 48 hours of signing.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you want to walk through the monitoring and fallback behavior.

Best,
